Solution B is correct. The only handshakes are between witches and sorcerers, and each of the 6 witches shakes hands with each of the 10 sorcerers. That gives 6 × 10 = 60 handshakes, which is the same as counting from the sorcerers' side (10 × 6 = 60).

Solution A goes wrong when it counts the sorcerers' handshakes. It says each sorcerer shook hands with the other sorcerers, then subtracts overlaps. But the problem says the sorcerers did not shake hands with each other, so they made no sorcerer-to-sorcerer handshakes to count. Each sorcerer's handshakes are only with the witches, so the sorcerers' total is 60, not 51. Adding that to the witches' 60 also counts every witch-sorcerer handshake twice, so even the 111 overcounts. Its 51 is not a valid count of anything in this scenario.

WINNER: B
